gaps.sentence: 'I'll see you tomorrow,' he said. He said he would see me ___.
gaps.explanation: Time expressions shift: tomorrow becomes the next day / the following day.

gaps.sentence: 'We may be a few minutes late,' they warned. They warned that they ___ be a few minutes late.
"Would you like a drink?" — He ___ me a drink.
'I have to catch the last train,' she said. She said she ___ catch the last train.
gaps.explanation: Have to (obligation) backshifts to had to after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'The road is being resurfaced,' the council said. The council said the road ___ resurfaced.
gaps.explanation: Present continuous passive (is being resurfaced) backshifts to past continuous passive: was being resurfaced.

gaps.sentence: 'The earth goes round the sun,' the teacher said. The teacher said that the earth ___ round the sun.
gaps.explanation: Timeless general truths may keep the present simple after a past reporting verb.

gaps.sentence: 'Why hasn't she replied?' he wondered. He wondered why she ___ replied.
gaps.explanation: hasn't replied → hadn't replied: statement order and past perfect.

gaps.sentence: 'Leave now or I'll call the police!' he shouted. He ___ to call the police.
gaps.explanation: A threatening conditional utterance is reported as threatened to do something.
